title: pseuderanthemum subviscosum
intro: Pseuderanthemum subviscosum, commonly known as False Hygrophila or Marsh Dewflower, is a species of flowering plant in the family Acanthaceae. This plant is traditionally used in Ayurvedic medicine, where it is valued for its potential health benefits, including its anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial properties. The therapeutic actions of Pseuderanthemum subviscosum are attributed to its bioactive constituents, which include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, that have been shown to exhibit anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial activities. The plant's bioactive constituents also exhibit potential therapeutic actions, including wound healing, anti-diabetic, and anti-cancer properties, although further research is needed to confirm these findings.
